nodeData.topic: Constitution of Kenya 2010 — article by article · draft
nodeData.note: Draft · review in progress. First draft, not yet reviewed by a lawyer. Do not rely on it for exams, court or advice. One map per chapter of the Constitution, one bubble per Article in plain words, each linked to the official text on the Kenya Law Reform Commission site (klrc.go.ke). Chapters 1–8 (Articles 1–128) so far; a new chapter is added every Friday. Search words: Katiba, Constitution of Kenya 2010, Bill of Rights, Article, Ibara.

Key terms, cases and rules: tap one to open the map that explains it.
Terms starting with A.
No torture, no slavery, fair trial, habeas corpus — never limited.
Citizens may access State-held information and information needed to protect a right.
Told why, may stay silent, advocate, court within 24 hours, bail unless compelling reasons.
Peaceably and unarmed.
Terms starting with B.
The Supreme Court held the doctrine does not apply in Kenya; amendment follows Chapter 16 only.
Tobacco regulations upheld; Article 10 values binding; public participation needed for regulations.

children.topic: Bill of Rights, who it binds (Art. 20)
children.note: All law, all State organs and all persons, including private persons.
Special and ordinary county Bills, mediation committees.
Terms starting with C.
Name, education, basics, protection, both parents; best interests paramount.
Either parent a citizen on the day of birth; foundlings under eight presumed citizens.
Seven years married to a citizen, or seven years lawful residence, or adoption.
Protected for present and future generations.
Avoid conflicts and demeaning the office; removal bars other State office.
290 constituencies; population quota; ±30% or ±40%; reviewed every 8–12 years. Eneo bunge, wadi.
Quality, information, safety and economic interests, compensation.
47 counties in the First Schedule; two distinct, inter-dependent levels of government.
Culture as the foundation of the nation; royalties to communities; indigenous seeds.
Terms starting with D.
Everyone must respect, uphold and defend it; an unconstitutional government is unlawful.
A citizen by birth keeps Kenyan citizenship on taking another.
Only citizens; State officers and the defence forces may not hold dual citizenship (judges and commissioners excepted).
Terms starting with E.
Independent commission that enforces Chapter 6; Leadership and Integrity Act (Art. 80).
Health, housing, food, water, social security, education; no denial of emergency treatment.
Filed within 28 days of the result, except presidential petitions (Article 140). Kesi ya uchaguzi.
Nobody may be denied emergency medical treatment.
State duties to the environment (mazingira), EIA and audits; everyone must help protect it.
Anyone may sue to protect the Article 42 right; no need to prove loss or injury.
No discrimination; affirmative action; no more than two-thirds of a body of one gender.
Terms starting with F.
Expeditious, efficient, lawful, reasonable, procedurally fair; written reasons.
Presumption of innocence, disclosure, interpreter, no double jeopardy, appeal; tainted evidence excluded.
Adults of the opposite sex, free consent, equal rights in and after marriage.
Excludes war propaganda, incitement, hate speech and advocacy of hatred.
Terms starting with G.
Two-thirds rule for Parliament to be realised progressively, legislation by 27 August 2015.
Two-thirds gender rule for Parliament progressive; measures by 27 August 2015.
Second Tuesday in August every fifth year; by-elections within 90 days. Tarehe ya uchaguzi.
Official gifts belong to the Republic; no foreign bank accounts except under an Act.
Terms starting with H.
A detained person may ask the court to test the detention; the right can never be limited.
Promotes and monitors human rights; anyone may complain; now split into KNCHR, NGEC and the Ombudsman.
Terms starting with I.
Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission: runs elections and referenda, registers voters, draws boundaries. Tume ya uchaguzi.
Out of any party for three months before the election, plus voter support (Article 99). Mgombea huru.
Terms starting with K.
Swahili for Constitution / Article — this library.
Terms starting with L.
Fair pay, reasonable conditions, trade unions, the right to strike, collective bargaining.
Parliament must revise land laws and legislate on acreage limits, matrimonial property and dependants.
Seven principles: fair access, secure rights, sustainable use, open administration, fragile areas, no gender bias, local dispute settlement. Ardhi.
Kiswahili, English and Kenyan Sign Language; see Article 7. Lugha.
Kiswahili is the national language; Kiswahili and English are official.
Office as a public trust: serve, not rule; integrity, impartiality, accountability. Uadilifu, maadili.
Only by law, reasonable and justifiable in an open and democratic society; five factors; State proves it.
Terms starting with M.
Integrity under Article 73 judged by an objective, evidence-based test.
No State control or penalties; independent licensing and standards body.
Citizenship by birth not lost by a foreign passport; cancellation and removal void.
Affirmative action, representation, water, health and infrastructure.
Taxes, public money, loans; starts only in the National Assembly. Mswada wa fedha, Finance Bill.
Who may stand and the eight disqualifications.
Terms starting with N.
290 + 47 women + 12 nominated = 349, plus the Speaker. Wabunge.
Madaraka 1 June, Mashujaa 20 October, Jamhuri 12 December.
Manages public land, advises on land policy and titles, investigates historical land injustices.
Patriotism, rule of law, participation, dignity, equity, integrity, transparency, accountability, sustainable development.
Concessions to exploit natural resources made from 27 Aug 2010 need Parliament's ratification.
Kenya has no official religion.
Non-citizens may only lease, up to 99 years; a company counts as a citizen only if wholly citizen-owned.
Terms starting with O.
No State office before the oath or affirmation (Third Schedule).
Participation, dignity, care from family and State.
Terms starting with P.
National Assembly and Senate; their separate roles. Bunge, Seneti.
Runs Parliament's services, staff and budget; chaired by the National Assembly Speaker. PSC.
Nominated and special seats by proportional representation; lists alternate men and women. Orodha ya chama.
Every citizen is entitled to a passport; it can be withheld only under an Act meeting Article 24.
Dignity, access, Sign language and Braille; at least five per cent in public bodies.
National character, internal democracy; no tribal or religious base, no militia, no bribery. Vyama vya siasa.
Free, fair and regular elections; every adult citizen may register, vote and stand.
14 days to sign or refer back; two-thirds to override; silence counts as assent.
Person, home, property, possessions, private information, communications.
Own property anywhere; compulsory acquisition only for a public purpose with prompt, full, just compensation.
Required before laws and regulations are made; Article 10(2) values are enforceable now (BAT v CS Health, 2019). Ushiriki wa umma.
Three classes of land; public land held in trust by counties or the nation; community land for communities; freehold and leasehold are private.
Terms starting with Q.
50 members in the National Assembly, 15 in the Senate.
Terms starting with R.
Voters may recall their MP or senator; grounds set by an Act.
Declaration, injunction, conservatory order, invalidity, compensation, judicial review.
Kenya is a sovereign, multi-party democratic Republic.
Only registered citizens and presumed foundlings; fraud, war, serious crime.
Life begins at conception; abortion only for emergency treatment or danger to the mother, or under another written law.
Terms starting with S.
Full-time State officers: no other paid work; appointed ones: no party office; pensioners: two posts at most.
No faith is official; works with Article 27 (no discrimination) and Article 32 (freedom of religion). Dini.
One vote per county on county matters; 24 of 47 needed.
47 + 16 women + 2 youth + 2 disability = 67, plus the Speaker. Maseneta.
All State power belongs to the people and is used only under the Constitution, directly or through elected representatives.
Anyone may sue, also for others, a group or the public interest; no filing fee.
14 days, extensions by the National Assembly, Supreme Court review.
The highest law; conflicting law is void to the extent of the clash; ratified treaties are part of Kenyan law.
Terms starting with T.
No elective body may be more than two-thirds one gender; for Parliament to be achieved progressively (Supreme Court 2012). Kanuni ya theluthi mbili.
Terms starting with V.
Adult citizen, not of unsound mind, no election offence in five years; one centre only. Usajili wa wapiga kura.
Terms starting with Y.
Education, participation, employment, protection.
